transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 09:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Maya (SummitHealth), Jon (SummitHealth Infra), Liam (SummitHealth Procurement)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're here for the renewal and expansion check-in for SummitHealth, happy to kick off. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Maya (SummitHealth): Hey, Maya here.
[00:14] Jon (SummitHealth): Jon on infra.
[00:16] Liam (SummitHealth): Liam from procurement.
[00:18] Ethan (Redwood): Ethan here, SE.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood): Priya joining as CSM.
[00:22] Sofia: Awesome. Quick recap — your current reserved capacity commit ends in mid-April, and we chatted last month about increasing committed GPU pools and adding eu-central-1 as a region. Today we wanted to align on timelines, benchmarks, and the contract term options — 12 vs 24 month.

[01:03] Maya: Yep that's right. Our main asks: one, we need more steady throughput for prediction workloads (peak is now about 30% higher than when we signed); two, latency-sensitive endpoints for EU patients so adding eu region is important; three, procurement wants clarity on pricing if we extend and bump capacity.

[01:40] Sofia: Great, that's consistent with what we saw in usage. Ethan, can you walk through options for capacity upgrade and multi-region setup?

[01:50] Ethan: Sure. Two main paths: increase reserved dedicated capacity in your current pool and add a second dedicated pool in eu-central-1, or use a hybrid approach — keep core reserved in us-west-2 and use burst / hosted fallback in eu while we bring dedicated online. The dedicated pool gives predictable throughput and is the cleanest for latency — KV cache stays local to pool, so fewer cold starts. Note: when we say KV cache some call it KV cash in transcripts, but it's the KV cache.

[02:35] Jon: When you say dedicated pool for eu — what are lead times? We have procurement windows.

[02:42] Ethan: Typical provisioning for reserved GPUs in a new region is 2-4 weeks once contracts are signed and payment cleared, could be quicker if we use available capacity. We'll need a sizing target from you — how many concurrent tokens/sec or qps is your target?

[03:05] Maya: Our P95 request latency needs to be ~200ms for the patient-facing triage endpoint. Throughput-wise, baseline is roughly 120 qps across models at peak; we can share the usage spreadsheet again.

[03:25] Ethan: That helps. For 120 qps with that latency target we recommend bumping to the next reserved tier — that's an extra 4 GPUs in the pool for dedicated inference, plus an option to enable burst capacity for spikes. That should cover headroom and keep cost predictable.

[03:46] Liam: How does pricing change for a 12 vs 24 month term? We prefer a discount if we lock in 24 months, but want flexibility on regions.

[03:58] Sofia: For 24 months we can apply a 10% discount on the reserved capacity line item, and we can structure a regional add-on as an amendment that gets priced per region and applied once provisioning starts. We'll send a three-option quote: 12-month, 24-month, and a 12+regional-commit option.

[04:20] Priya: Also happy to include a usage credit buffer for the first month of region bring-up to offset any inefficiencies during warm-up.

[04:30] Maya: That would help. Another ask: we need to ensure all data at rest is encrypted with our KMS and logs go into our SIEM. Can you confirm the Private deployment or Dedicated has KMS integration?

[04:45] Ethan: Yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS; we have HSM/Cloud KMS integrations documented. For logs, we can forward audit logs to your SIEM via the log-forwarder. We'll share network diagrams and the SOC2 report.

[05:05] Jon: On the network diagrams — are we able to route traffic over a VPC peering or is it a transit gateway requirement? We want the minimal public egress.

[05:16] Ethan: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on your cloud and topology. We'll provide the standard config we've used with other customers; sometimes there's minor adjustments.

[05:28] Liam: Procurement will need the amendment language for region adds and also a cap on price increases.

[05:35] Sofia: We can provide amendment language and a pricing cap clause for the initial 12 months after the amendment — that's standard for reserved upgrades. We'll have legal review drafts ready.

[06:00] Maya: One technical caveat — we're running a custom quantized model variant. Any special considerations for model loading time and KV cache warm up when we move traffic across regions?

[06:18] Ethan: Yes, quantized models can have different cold start times. We recommend pre-warming key models in the EU pool using a warmup script; we can run that as part of onboarding. Also ensure your model artifacts are replicated to the region's storage to avoid network pulls.

[06:42] Maya: Okay. For benchmarks — can you do a realistic run with our prompt shapes and token distributions? We have a small replica dataset.

[06:50] Ethan: Absolutely. If you share a sanitized subset and target prompt shapes we'll run a 50k-token/day sim across the dedicated pool and report p95/p99 latency, throughput, and token cost.

[07:06] Priya: I'll follow up with the upload link.

[07:10] Sofia: Great. On SLAs — you're currently on the standard Dedicated SLA with uptime and latency SLOs. For enterprise we can discuss a more specific SLA tied to the reserved pool in EU with credits if missed. Is that something you want in the amendment?

[07:27] Liam: Yes, procurement wants explicit SLA for EU endpoints once live.

[07:32] Sofia: Noted. We'll draft amendment language with an SLA clause for the EU pool and associated credits.

[07:40] Jon: Are there any known performance trade-offs if we enable stronger encryption or end-to-end TLS with client-side certs?

[07:48] Ethan: Minimal — TLS termination and KMS calls add small overhead; the main impact is on startup and slightly higher CPU for encryption. In most configs it doesn't push you over the latency target for the sizes you're describing, but we'll measure in benchmarks.

[08:02] Maya: Okay. A quick question on fallbacks: if our EU pool has a transient outage, what's the cross-region fallback behavior? We want graceful degradation, not full outage.

[08:14] Ethan: We can configure smart routing — route by latency first, but with automatic fallback to your us-west-2 pool. You can set policy to failover at P95 > X ms or on specific error classes. Keep in mind cross-region calls will add network latency.

[08:31] Sofia: To summarize, action items: Redwood to send updated pricing and amendment language; SE to run benchmark in us-west-2 and provision test in eu-central when ready; customer to confirm term and region list.

[08:45] Maya: Sounds good. Anything else on procurement or billing?
[08:50] Liam: Just one: can we get an invoicing cadence option quarterly vs monthly for the reserved commitment?

[08:56] Sofia: Yes — invoicing cadence is configurable on enterprise contracts; we'll include both options in the quote.

[09:05] Priya: I'll share the security pack and a pointer to the SOC2 report after this call.

[09:10] Maya: Thanks.
[09:12] Sofia: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the price decks and the benchmark scheduling.
[09:18] Liam: Thanks all.
[09:20] Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript contains minor transcription errors typical of call exports (product names sometimes mis-heard, punctuation inconsistent). References to KV cache, VPC, KMS, HSM, Private/Dedicated are present. Shared artifacts: pricing deck (link to be sent), SOC2 report (link to be shared), benchmark spreadsheet (customer will upload).
